verdicts.quote: Build metadata MUST be ignored when determining version precedence. Thus two versions that differ only in the build metadata, have the same precedence. Examples: 1.0.0-alpha+001, 1.0.0+20130313144700, 1.0.0-beta+exp.sha.5114f85, 1.0.0+21AF26D3----117B344092BD.
verdicts.note: The page states the general rule the claim rests on (build metadata is ignored for precedence, so versions differing only in build metadata have the same precedence), and the spec title 'Semantic Versioning 2.0.0' is present. But the specific pair 1.0.0+001 and 1.0.0+002 does not appear, and the page says such versions have the same PRECEDENCE, not that they are 'the same version' — clause 3 ('the contents of that version MUST NOT be modified') and the grammar treat build metadata as part of the version string. Weaker/narrower version of the claim only.

verdicts.quote: Numeric identifiers MUST NOT include leading zeroes.
verdicts.note: The page states the prohibition only for numeric identifiers: the version core ("X, Y, and Z are non-negative integers, and MUST NOT contain leading zeroes") and numeric pre-release identifiers. It does not extend it to every identifier: the build metadata rule requires only ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens and non-emptiness, the BNF allows <build identifier> ::= <digits> (which permits leading zeroes), and the page's own example 1.0.0-alpha+001 is given as valid. So the narrower claim is stated; the universal 'every identifier' version is not.

verdicts.quote: Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, increment the: MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes
verdicts.note: The page's Summary states the claim verbatim, and item 8 of the specification restates it as a normative rule: "Major version X (X.y.z | X > 0) MUST be incremented if any backward incompatible changes are introduced to the public API."

verdicts.quote: Pre-release versions have a lower precedence than the associated normal version.
verdicts.note: The page states the opposite of the claim. Item 9 of the specification says pre-release versions have LOWER precedence than the associated normal version, and the precedence section repeats it: "When major, minor, and patch are equal, a pre-release version has lower precedence than a normal version: Example: 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0."

verdicts.quote: No, “v1.2.3” is not a semantic version. However, prefixing a semantic version with a “v” is a common way (in English) to indicate it is a version number.
verdicts.note: The page's FAQ explicitly asks "Is “v1.2.3” a semantic version?" and answers no; the BNF grammar likewise starts a valid semver at <version core> with no leading "v". The claim is directly incompatible with the source.
